title.narrative: Strengthening of quality infrastructure in the countries of Central Asia
Stärkung der Qualitätsinfrastrukturen in den Ländern Zentralasiens

description.narrative: Der mit der Auflösung der Sowjetunion begonnene Transformationsprozess von einem planwirtschaftlichen zu einem marktwirtschaftlichen System prägt nach wie vor die wirtschaftliche Entwicklung der zentralasiatischen Staaten. Dies betrifft unter anderem die Integration in den internationalen Handel und den Aufbau von Wertschöpfungsketten, die international wettbewerbsfähig sind. Die zentralasiatischen Staaten suchen verstärkt den Zugang zu internationalen Märkten. Eine effiziente und nachhaltige Teilnahme am internationalen Handel erfordert die Implementierung einer inter-national anerkannten Qualitätsinfrastruktur (Metrologie, Akkreditierung, Normung, Konformitätsbewertung), um eine international vergleichbare Bewertung der Qualitätsmerkmale von Waren und Dienstleistungen zu ermöglichen. Das Kernproblem besteht darin, dass die Institutionen der Qualitätsinfrastruktur der zentralasiatischen Länder bisher noch nicht in ausreichendem Maße in der Lage sind, Dienstleistungen anzubieten, die den internationalen Anforderungen entsprechen. Der Abbau technischer Handelshemmnisse und die Teilnahme am internationalen Wettbewerb wird dadurch gehemmt, dass eine international vergleich-bare Qualitätssicherung bislang nicht implementiert und nachgewiesen werden kann.

The process of transformation that began with the resolution of the Soviet Union from a planned economy to a market economy system continues to shape the economic development of the Central Asian states. This concerns, inter alia, the integration into international economy and the development of value chains that are internationally competitive. The Central Asian states are increasingly looking for access to international markets. Efficient and sustainable participation in international trade requires the implementation of an internationally recognized quality infrastructure (metrology, accreditation, standardization, conformity assessment) in order to enable an internationally comparable assessment of the quality characteristics of goods and services. It can therefore be identified as a key problem that the national institutions of the quality infrastructure in Central Asia do not yet meet international requirements. There are internationally recognized rules for the functioning of Quality Infrastructure institutions that have not yet been introduced. The countries of Central Asia therefore only participate in world trade to a small extent. The key problem is that the institutions of the quality infrastructure of the Central Asian countries are not yet able to offer services that meet international requirements. The dismantling of technical barriers to trade and participation in international competition is hampered by the fact that an internationally comparable quality assurance system has not yet been implemented and proven.
Die Institutionen der Qualitätsinfrastruktur bieten verstärkt nachfrageorientierte Dienstleistungen zur Qualitätssicherung nach internationalen Standards für die Wirtschaft an

The project aims at strengthening quality infrastructure institutions in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan to offer demand-oriented services for quality assurance in the economy in accordance with international standards

Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)

Due to the regional character of the project there is no lead institution provided. Implementing partners are the national metrology institutes and national accreditation bodies:
?Kazakhstan: Committee of Technical Regulation and Metrology of the Ministry of Trade and Integration of the Republic of Kazakhstan
?Kyrgyz Republic: Ministry of Economy of the Kyrgyz Republic
?Uzbekistan: Uzbek Agency for Standardization, Metrology and Certification ?Uzstandart Agency?
?Tajikistan: Ministry of Economy, Agency of Standardization, Metrology, Certification and Trade Inspection under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan ?Tajikstandart", Center for Accreditation (expected to be independent of "Tajikstandart" from 2017)
?Turkmenistan: State Etalon Centre under the Main State Service ?Turkmenstandartlary?
